title: TencentCloud/CubeSandbox — Instant, Concurrent, Secure & Lightweight Sandbox for AI Agents.

Cube Sandbox is a high-performance, out-of-the-box secure sandbox service built on RustVMM and KVM. It supports both single-node deployment and easy scaling to multi-node clusters. It is compatible with the E2B SDK and can create a hardware-isolated, fully serviceable sandbox in under 60ms with less than 5MB of memory overhead.
  
  
In the context of AI Agent code execution, CubeSandbox achieves the perfect balance of security and performance:
- Cold start benchmarked on bare-metal. 60ms at single concurrency; under 50 concurrent creations, avg 67ms, P95 90ms, P99 137ms — consistently sub-150ms.
- Memory overhead measured with sandbox specs ≤ 32GB. Larger configurations may see a marginal increase.
For detailed metrics on startup latency and resource overhead, see the Core Operations Performance Benchmark Report (bare metal) and the PVM Cloud Server Benchmark Report.
  
  ⚡ Millisecond-level startup — watch the fast-start flow above.
Cube Sandbox requires an x86_64 Linux environment with KVM support.
The guide walks you through everything in four steps — provisioning a server, installing Cube Sandbox, creating a sandbox template, and running your first agent code. No source build needed, up and running in minutes.

First thing after install: open the Web console
  
  🖥️ Visual management — from overview to creating a sandbox and streaming logs, all in your browser.
After one-click deployment, open in your browser:
http://<control-node IP>:12088
Recommended three steps:
- Check overview — Open Overview, confirm nodes are Ready and capacity looks healthy
- Prepare a template — Install an official preset from Template Store; skip if you already have a READY template under Templates
- Create a sandbox — Sandboxes → + New sandbox, pick a READY template, and view live logs on the detail page within seconds

report.summary: Tencent Cloud's CubeSandbox is a lightweight RustVMM/KVM-based sandbox service that launches secure AI agent environments in under 60ms.
report.background: AI agents increasingly need fast, isolated, on-demand code execution environments, but many existing sandboxes suffer from slow cold starts, high memory overhead, or weak isolation. CubeSandbox addresses this by building on RustVMM and KVM to provide hardware-virtualized, lightweight sandboxes tailored for AI agent workloads. It supports both single-node and multi-node cluster deployment, and its API compatibility with the E2B SDK makes it easy for existing agent platforms to adopt. The project is open-sourced under Apache License 2.0, is listed in the CNCF Landscape, and leverages mature virtualization components such as Cloud Hypervisor, Kata Containers, virtiofsd, and containerd-shim-rs. By prioritising millisecond-level startup and minimal resource footprint, CubeSandbox positions itself as infrastructure purpose-built for interactive and concurrent agent execution.
key_points: CubeSandbox achieves sub-60ms cold start on bare-metal hardware, with P99 latency of 137ms even under 50 concurrent sandbox creations. This makes real-time, interactive AI agent workflows far more practical than traditional VM-based isolation.

Each sandbox consumes less than 5MB of memory overhead while still providing hardware-level isolation through RustVMM and KVM. That combination is rare: most secure sandboxes require far more resources, while lighter-weight alternatives often rely on weaker process-level isolation.

The service is compatible with the E2B SDK, meaning developers currently using E2B for AI code execution can switch or integrate CubeSandbox with minimal changes. This compatibility lowers migration costs and expands the reach of the platform immediately.

CubeSandbox supports both single-node and multi-node cluster deployment. A built-in web console provides visual management for templates, sandbox lifecycle, and live logs, reducing the operational friction of running an agent infrastructure from the command line.

It is released under Apache License 2.0 and built on proven open-source virtualization components like Cloud Hypervisor and Kata Containers. The project is also listed in the CNCF Landscape, giving enterprises confidence in its long-term maintainability and community governance.
report.impact: CubeSandbox represents a push toward ultra-low-latency, secure sandboxes as a standard layer for AI agent code execution. For the AI industry, it lowers the performance penalty of isolating untrusted code, potentially enabling more autonomous and interactive agents that execute actions repeatedly without stalling. Developers benefit from an open, E2B-compatible pathway to hardware-isolated sandboxes with sub-100ms startup, making it easier to build hosted tools, coding assistants, or agent frameworks. Regular users will experience faster response times and more safety when an AI handles tasks like browsing, scripting, or data manipulation, because the underlying execution environment can spin up almost instantly and keep untrusted code confined. Becoming CNCF-listed and Apache-licensed may also accelerate standardisation of sandbox APIs in the broader agent ecosystem.
report.tools: To follow up or experiment with CubeSandbox, watch the GitHub repository (TencentCloud/CubeSandbox) and its Quick Start guide. For ecosystem context, keep an eye on E2B, which CubeSandbox is SDK-compatible with. Developers interested in internals should also track Cloud Hypervisor, Kata Containers, virtiofsd, and containerd-shim-rs — the open-source components it builds upon.
